1#_: (Siman 101 seif 1 in the hagahah) And if it is a doubt whether it is a piece worthy of honor, we follow the lenient view. The Taz's words here require study — he wrote regarding non-Jewish cheeses that they are not nullified because they are worthy of honor unless known they were not curdled in neveilah stomach, implying even a doubt of basar b'chalav forbids them. I did not understand his conclusion, for it is a doubt whether forbidden on account of itself — most poskim hold non-Jewish cheese is not forbidden because of stomach curdling. Taz himself in siman 81 is lenient on doubtful treifah milk cheese. Peri Megadim explains Taz as dealing when there is not sixty against the stomach — still puzzling. See Beit Yosef siman 115 and Peri Chadash.
2#_: (Seif 2 in the hagahah) Every piece forbidden only on account of a peel is nullified, for a peel is not worthy of honor. Shach cites Lev Chaim: why forbidden on account of itself if it absorbed from another prohibition? And in Minchat Shai he left it requiring study. It can be forbidden on account of itself at the cut site — see Gemara regarding the fetus extending its hand, and detached limb siman 55. Cooking on Shabbat forbidden only on account of a peel is an example. Shach's case of hot meat into cold milk requiring sixty against the peel is difficult for those who hold dry nullification — see siman 105. Piece forbidden on account of peel nullifies in dry majority — Mordechai, Rabeinu Yerucham, Beit Yosef siman 105.
3#_: (Seif 3) And a whole sheep, etc. is not considered worthy of honor. See Chavat Daat who proved from Pesachim that a whole sheep is not nullified and is a piece worthy of honor — five Paschal hides mixed, a blemish found, all go to burning and require a second Pesach even before sprinkling, because at sprinkling time they were not fit. If a whole sheep is not nullified, this is difficult. Answer: they are forbidden because of invalid emurim mixed, not because of meat mixture — what is offered on the altar is not nullified; therefore they require second Pesach d'oraisa. Chavat Daat's rejection is answered. See Yad Malachi and Noda BiYehudah siman 16 on effort like chicken in feathers.
4#_: (Seif 6 in the hagahah) And there is no distinction whether mixed in its kind or not in its kind. It may be not in its kind, e.g. fish kinds with the same appearance — siman 83 seif 4. Or Zarua and Derishah disagree whether cut fish are one kind; the hagahah follows that cut pieces can be two kinds — Gemara in Pesachim supports this. Peri Chadash on siman 98 agrees with Or Zarua for whole fish; cut fish may remain two kinds by name — see Tosefet Yom Tov on kilayim regarding camel wool with sheep wool.
